intro:

sections.heading: Astrology in one page
sections.html:
Astrology doesn’t say what will happen; it outlines what tends to happen when energies combine. Think weather, not fate. Your birth chart maps planetary positions into twelve houses. Each planet expresses through a zodiac sign and lands in a house, then forms geometric angles (aspects) with other planets. Reading the chart is connecting these four layers with context.

  • Planets = drives/agents (e.g., Mars acts, Venus bonds, Mercury thinks).
  • Signs = style (e.g., Aries acts fast, Taurus stabilizes, Gemini connects).
  • Houses = life areas (e.g., 1st self, 7th partnership, 10th career/public role).
  • Aspects = relationship between parts (e.g., Sun trine Moon is harmony; Mars square Venus is spice/tension).

sections.heading: Zodiac signs: the “how” of expression
sections.html:
Signs are twelve flavors of behavior. They’re not boxes; they’re styles your planets use. For example, Mars in Scorpio pursues with depth and strategy; Mars in Aries charges head-on. Start with your big three: Sun (vitality), Moon (needs), and Rising/Ascendant (chart angle in the 1st house).

sections.heading: Planets: the “who/what” acting in the chart
sections.html:
Each planet represents a core function. The sign shows how that function behaves; the house shows where it plays out. Examples: Sun in Leo in the 10th house reads as public creativity; Moon in Cancer in the 4th house craves rooted, home-centered safety.

sections.heading: Houses: the “where” (twelve arenas of life)
sections.html:
The houses are twelve slices of life. Planet-in-house tells you where energy shows up. Example: Venus in the 5th house loves play and romance; Saturn in the 10th demands slow, solid career-building.

1st: Self, identity, start lines2nd: Money, skills, values3rd: Mindset, siblings, local4th: Home, roots, parents5th: Play, creativity, dating6th: Habits, health, service7th: Partners, contracts8th: Merging, intimacy, fear9th: Travel, belief, meaning10th: Career, status, legacy11th: Friends, networks, causes12th: Retreat, dreams, undoing

sections.heading: Aspects: harmony and tension between parts
sections.html:
Aspects are angles between planets measured on the wheel. They show how one part of you “talks” to another. A trine is like a greased runway; a square is a corner you must turn; an opposition asks for balance. Example reads: Sun trine Moon (inner/outer in sync), Mars square Venus (desire vs. harmony), Mercury opposition Neptune (facts vs. fantasy).

AspectMeaning (short)
Conjunction (0°)Merge of functions—loud, focused, fused
Sextile (60°)Opportunity with light effort; ask and it opens
Square (90°)Friction that builds muscle; turn the corner
Trine (120°)Ease/flow; use it or snooze it
Opposition (180°)Polarity; negotiate the seesaw

sections.heading: Common chart types (what to use when)
sections.html:
Different charts answer different questions. Start with your base map, then layer technique.

  • Birth/Natal chart: your base map. Make one here → /birth-chart
  • Synastry chart (two charts compared): for relationship dynamics → /compatibility
  • Transit chart: current planetary weather across your chart → see astrology charts
  • Composite chart: the relationship as a single entity → overview at /astrology-charts

sections.heading: Timing techniques: transits, retrogrades, moons
sections.html:
Astrological timing watches how the current sky activates your natal placements. Transits show triggers and seasons; retrogrades mark review cycles; lunations (new/full moons) set monthly tone.

  • Transits: track Jupiter growth years, Saturn tests, Uranus shake-ups. See charts → /astrology-charts
  • Retrogrades: rethink and repair (e.g., Mercury Rx for comms) → /retrogrades
  • Moons: monthly reset/release work → /moons

sections.heading: How to read your chart (simple sequence)
sections.html:
1. Get the data right: exact birth time/place → make your chart here: /birth-chart
  2. Big three: read your Sun, Moon, and Rising (Ascendant in 1st house) via their signs/houses.
  3. Chart backbone: note the 4th/10th (home/career) and 1st/7th (self/other) axes.
  4. Aspects: identify 3–5 major aspects (e.g., Sun trine Moon, Mars square Venus).
  5. Story it: turn notes into a paragraph: Planet in Sign in House, themed by Aspects.
  6. Apply: align habits in the 6th house and goals in the 10th.

sections.heading: Compatibility: beyond sun-sign memes
sections.html:
Real relationship astrology compares two full charts (synastry). Sun signs set tone, but Moon to Moon (Moon needs), Venus/Mars (Venus bonding, Mars desire), and angles (1st/7th) carry the weight. Start here → /compatibility.

  • Fire + air often flow (e.g., Leo with Libra); earth + water often nurture (e.g., Taurus with Cancer).
  • Squares/oppositions aren’t doom. Mars square Venus can be hot if respect is mutual.
  • House overlays matter: their planets in your 7th house (partnership) or 5th (romance) change the feel.

sections.heading: Myths, limits, and ethics
sections.html:
• Not mind-reading, not destiny: astrology offers patterns and timing, not certainties.
  • Context rules: the same transit lands differently in different lives. Your choices matter.
  • Consent and care: share readings with respect. Don’t diagnose; don’t scare.
  • Usefulness test: if an interpretation doesn’t help action, reframe it.

faqs.q: Do I need my exact birth time?
faqs.a: It sharpens accuracy—especially the Ascendant and houses. If unknown, try records or family recall; you can still read planets-in-sign and some aspects via your birth chart .

faqs.q: What’s the difference between Sun sign and rising sign?
faqs.a: Sun = core direction ( Sun ). Rising = how you move through the world (the sign on the 1st house ). Both matter; so does the Moon .
Neither. Trines flow but can get lazy; squares are work but build skill. Read specifics (e.g., Sun trine Moon vs. Mercury square Saturn ).
Read your planets → signs → houses → aspects in that order. Use our hubs: signs , planets , houses , aspects .

faqs.q: How do I use astrology day-to-day?
faqs.a: Track transits to your 6th house for habits and to your 10th for career moves. Note lunations and any strong aspects to your Sun / Moon .
